items.question: What is your leadership and management style when leading engineering teams?
items.answer: My leadership style is servant and context-driven. I focus on setting clear architectural guardrails and business objectives while giving engineers autonomy on execution. I run weekly 1-on-1s for unblocking and growth, conduct blameless post-mortems to foster psychological safety, and advocate for engineering health through continuous refactoring cycles alongside product delivery.

items.question: Describe a challenging system design problem you solved and how you scaled it.
items.answer: At SiamFin, our payment reconciliation was taking 4+ hours due to batch DB locking. I redesigned the pipeline into an event-driven architecture using Apache Kafka and FastAPI workers with Redis idempotency keys. This decoupled transaction ingestion from settlement verification, handling 3.5M daily transactions in near-real-time (<30s lag) with zero data loss or double processing.

items.question: What is your notice period and when can you start?
items.answer: My standard notice period is 30 calendar days from the date an official offer is signed. All handover materials and documentation are kept up-to-date to ensure a smooth transition.

items.question: What are your salary expectations for this role?
items.answer: My target compensation is 150,000 to 170,000 THB per month, open to negotiation depending on the total package, health benefits, annual bonus structure, and remote work flexibility.

items.question: How do you handle technical disagreements or conflicts with peers or product managers?
items.answer: I ground technical debates in empirical data and user impact rather than ego. When disagreeing on architecture, I write a lightweight RFC highlighting tradeoffs, benchmarks, and maintenance cost. For product-engineering misalignments, I clarify the core business constraint and propose iterative compromises (e.g., shipping a minimal viable feature first, then hardening under load).
